reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a 600-plus FTM and tenfold-return claim alongside instructions to deploy a contract, connect a wallet, send 98 FTM or more, and execute a transaction. The description includes a general warning about flash-loan exploits, but the promoted participation flow ties the claimed return to a cryptocurrency transfer.

citations.quote: Huge Profits! (600+ FTM +) FANTOM Flash Loan Arbitrage Trading Bot | 10X with FTM Flash Loan
Send FTM to the deployed contract to initiate the swap
Now I need to supply this contract slash coin with enough gas to be able to arbitrage trade back and forth with itself.
we only made like 1200
Eventually, these decks will make it so we can't do this. But it's working now, guys. And I mean, it's sweet. It's easy. It's fast.

opening.argument: The material is better understood as a warning-aware demonstration than deceptive solicitation. Its description expressly acknowledges that flash-loan exploits have been used to attack vulnerable protocols and steal millions, making the risks part of the presentation rather than concealing them. The speaker also explains that the process depends on rapidly trading against a particular exchange and admits that changing market conditions may end it. That qualification is inconsistent with presenting an assured or universally repeatable return. The claimed result is presented as the creator's own experience, while viewers are given technical context and an explicit risk signal.

citations.quote: While they've proved popular, flash loan exploits have been used to attack vulnerable DeFi protocols and steal millions of dollars.
Eventually, these decks will make it so we can't do this.
we only made like 1200

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title's promotional wording and the funding instructions do not erase the material's warning context. Saying to send FTM to a contract establishes a technical step, not that the creator concealed risk or guaranteed a viewer's result. The speaker expressly says the opportunity may disappear, so the prosecution's reading treats a conditional demonstration as a certainty.

citations.quote: flash loan exploits have been used to attack vulnerable DeFi protocols and steal millions of dollars.
Eventually, these decks will make it so we can't do this.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warning about exploits concerns attacks on vulnerable protocols, not a warning that viewers may lose the FTM the instructions tell them to send. The uncertainty about future availability does not qualify the immediate earnings presentation: the title says “Huge Profits!” and “10X,” while the speaker says the result was “$1400” and calls the process easy and fast.

citations.quote: Huge Profits! (600+ FTM +) FANTOM Flash Loan Arbitrage Trading Bot | 10X with FTM Flash Loan
That's $1400
It's easy. It's fast.

opening.argument: The video's central activity is an operational walkthrough of blockchain development and arbitrage mechanics. It sets up a Remix workspace, compiles a Solidity contract, connects MetaMask through injected Web3, deploys the contract, and explains why a self-created token is used. Those are concrete programming and tool-use steps, not merely an invitation to purchase an opaque product. The speaker demonstrates his own transaction sequence and explains the technical dependency on flash-loan trading. A tutorial can show a successful example without certifying that every viewer will reproduce the same outcome.

citations.quote: we need a new workspace inside remix.ethereum.org.
My solidity compiler version is 0.5.16
we got to deploy our own token or contract on the FTM chain.
Then we're going to get a flash loan to trade that against Zootre.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The evidence supports a technical tutorial framing: the description supplies numbered setup steps, and the narration explains the contract, compiler, network, and trading sequence. The fact that the demonstration includes a result does not convert every coding instruction into a financial guarantee. The prosecution identifies persuasive language, but does not show that the programming content is a pretext for an undisclosed service.

Once again, links in the video description.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Technical instructions are precisely what make the promotion actionable: the description tells viewers to deploy the contract, send FTM, and click “flashloan.” The tutorial framing does not change that the speaker links the workflow to profits, says the result was about $1,200, and calls it easy and fast. Coding detail shows how to participate; it does not establish neutral education.

Now, Click "flashloan" (red box) to execute the Flash Loan.
we only made like 1200
It's easy. It's fast.

opening.argument: The record does not show several hallmark mechanisms of a conventional scam. There is no request for passwords, seed phrases, account credentials, recruitment, downline income, or payment for access to a seller's custody service. Instead, the described activity is an on-chain arbitrage experiment using a contract, a flash loan, and exchange swaps. The instructions identify the tools and transaction stages rather than asking viewers to trust an invisible operator. Even the requested FTM is described as gas supplied to the deployed contract, not a deposit into a personal account or a fee for guaranteed returns.

citations.quote: Now I need to supply this contract slash coin with enough gas to be able to arbitrage trade back and forth with itself.
We'll deploy a new smart contract to the Fantom FTM Chain using remix and swap tokens on Pancakeswap and Uniswap.
Send FTM to the deployed contract to initiate the swap

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the FTM “gas” does not make the mechanism ordinary commerce, but it does matter that the funds are tied to a disclosed contract workflow rather than an alleged custodial investment account. The material also names the exchanges and explains the intended swap process. No credential request or recruitment scheme appears in the supplied evidence, so the prosecution must rely on inference from the existence of a transfer.

citations.quote: enough gas to be able to arbitrage trade back and forth with itself.
Then we're going to get a flash loan to trade that against Zootre.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of passwords or recruitment is not dispositive because the relevant mechanism is a funded contract tied to a profit claim. The instructions specifically tell viewers to send 98 FTM or more, and the speaker says the wallet result was about $1,200. Calling the transfer gas describes its stated purpose, but does not establish that viewers will recover it or earn the advertised return.
